items.text: Julia — could you walk me through the expected lift and timeline for the joint product launches you’re planning to tie into the co‑branded campaigns? I need to model the incremental spend and ROI, and I want to make sure our assumptions line up before we lock anything in. I’m drafting the budget in the restricted folder, so please keep any details within this thread until we have a final sign‑off.

Ingrid — here’s the high‑level view for the joint launches: 

*Product A* – launch scheduled for early Feb 2026; we anticipate a 12 % incremental revenue lift. Campaign spend allocated: $150 K in Feb, with a projected ROI of ~1.8×. 

*Product B* – rollout planned for mid‑Mar 2026; expected lift is 8 % and $200 K of spend in Mar, ROI ~1.6×. 

The remaining $150 K will support post‑launch amplification in Apr, covering both products. All assumptions are documented in the draft budget stored in the restricted folder; please keep any further discussion confined to this thread until we obtain final sign‑off.

Julia — thanks for the high‑level numbers. To make sure my model aligns, could you share the underlying assumptions behind the 12 % lift for Product A and the 8 % lift for Product B (e.g., market size, price elasticity, channel mix), and also break out the post‑launch amplification spend in April—what mix of media and expected incremental impact are you assuming? I’ll keep everything in the restricted folder until we get sign‑off.

The 12 % lift for Product A assumes a $45 M addressable market in North‑America, a price‑elasticity coefficient of –1.3, and a channel mix of 55 % digital display, 30 % paid social, and 15 % programmatic video, yielding an estimated incremental revenue of $5.4 M; the 8 % lift for Product B is based on a $38 M market, elasticity of –1.1, and a mix of 60 % digital display, 25 % paid social, 15 % email nurture, projecting $3.0 M incremental revenue. For April’s $150 K amplification we allocate $70 K to retargeting display, $45 K to sponsored social carousel ads, $20 K to influencer micro‑content, and $15 K to post‑launch email drip, which together are modeled to add roughly 3 % incremental revenue across both products. All underlying data and calculation sheets remain in the restricted folder; please keep this discussion confined to this thread until final sign‑off.

Julia — thanks for the detailed breakdown; that gives me a solid base to start threading the financial model. Before I lock anything in, could you walk me through the exact ROI calc you used for each spend bucket (e.g., the lift attribution assumptions, the cost‑per‑acquisition inputs, and any discounting you applied), and also flag any high‑risk levers where a modest shift in the channel mix or elasticity could swing the projected return by more than 10 %? I’ll paste the numbers into the spreadsheet in the restricted folder and keep the discussion confined here until we get the final sign‑off.

Ingrid — the ROI for each spend bucket is derived by attributing the projected incremental revenue to the spend and applying a 5 % discount rate to reflect cash‑flow timing. For Product A: $150 K spend in Feb, incremental revenue $5.4 M, lift attribution 70 % to display, 20 % to paid social, 10 % to video; CPA $27.8; ROI ≈ 1.8× after discounting. For Product B: $200 K spend in Mar, incremental revenue $3.0 M, lift attribution 65 % display, 25 % paid social, 10 % email; CPA $30; ROI ≈ 1.6×. April amplification $150 K broken into $70 K retargeting, $45 K social carousel, $20 K influencer, $15 K email; incremental revenue ≈ 3 % of combined baseline (~$260 K), yielding ROI ≈ 1.7×. High‑risk levers: a 5‑point shift in channel mix (e.g., reducing display from 55 % to 50 % for Product A) or a 0.1 change in elasticity moves projected ROI by >10 %; similarly, CPA assumptions +/- 15 % have the same effect. All calculations and source tables remain in the restricted folder; please keep this discussion confined here until final sign‑off.

## Summary

This draft outlines the $500,000 allocation for the co‑branded campaigns, detailing spend by product, ROI assumptions, and high‑risk levers for final sign‑off.

## 1. Executive Overview

Ingrid Fontaine (Financial Analyst) and Julia Kim (Product Manager) have prepared a budget model for the joint marketing effort, targeting Product A (early Feb 2026 launch) and Product B (mid‑Mar 2026 rollout). The total spend of $500,000 is earmarked for media execution, post‑launch amplification, and contingency. This draft lives in the restricted folder and is pending review by Felix Reyes (VP of Operations).

## 2. Allocation Detail by Phase

The spend plan follows the high‑level breakdown previously shared:

- **Product A – Feb 2026:** $150,000 allocated to a channel mix of 55 % digital display, 30 % paid social, and 15 % programmatic video. Expected incremental revenue $5.4 M based on a $45 M addressable market and –1.3 elasticity.
- **Product B – Mar 2026:** $200,000 supporting 60 % digital display, 25 % paid social, and 15 % email nurture, projecting $3.0 M incremental revenue from a $38 M market with –1.1 elasticity.
- **April 2026 Amplification:** $150,000 split as $70,000 retargeting display, $45,000 sponsored social carousel, $20,000 influencer micro‑content, and $15,000 post‑launch email drip, modeled to lift combined revenue by roughly 3 % (~$260 K).

All line‑item codes and justification tables are stored in the restricted folder for audit.

## 3. ROI Calculations & Risk Levers

ROI is derived by attributing the projected incremental revenue to each spend bucket and applying a 5 % discount rate for cash‑flow timing:

- **Product A:** $150 K spend yields an ROI of ≈1.8 × after discounting (CPA $27.8). Lift attribution: 70 % display, 20 % paid social, 10 % video.
- **Product B:** $200 K spend yields an ROI of ≈1.6 × (CPA $30). Attribution: 65 % display, 25 % paid social, 10 % email.
- **April Amplification:** $150 K spend delivers an ROI of ≈1.7 ×, based on the 3 % incremental revenue estimate.

High‑risk levers identified by Julia Kim include a ±5‑point shift in channel mix (e.g., dropping display for Product A from 55 % to 50 %) or a ±0.1 change in elasticity, each of which can swing ROI by more than 10 %. CPA variations of ±15 % also trigger similar sensitivity.

These risk scenarios are documented in the attached sensitivity matrix (restricted folder).

## 4. Review, Sign‑off & Confidentiality

The draft budget is currently pending Felix Reyes (VP of Operations) review. Upon his approval, the document will be moved from the restricted folder to the final‑review copy for executive sign‑off. All stakeholders are reminded to keep any discussion of the $500,000 allocation, line‑item breakdowns, and ROI assumptions within the restricted folder until the formal sign‑off is recorded. No decision has been made at this stage; the next actionable step is the sign‑off meeting scheduled for early next week.
